MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Sex: Male
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRAL INFORMATION
Referring Physician: Dr. [redacted name]
Referral Reason: Diagnostic testing for Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Clinical Information: Pediatric male patient with clinical suspicion of dystrophinopathy

TEST PERFORMED
Multiplex Ligation-dependent Probe Amplification (MLPA) Analysis of DMD Gene

METHODOLOGY
MLPA analysis was performed using MRC-Holland SALSA MLPA probemix P034-B3 DMD-1 and P035-B2 DMD-2 kits according to manufacturer's protocols. These kits contain probes for all 79 exons of the DMD gene and the alternate promoter DP427C. DNA was extracted from peripheral blood using standard procedures. MLPA products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3730xl DNA Analyzer. Data analysis was performed using Coffalyser.Net software. Gene dosage quotients between 0.7 and 1.3 were considered normal. Values <0.7 indicate deletion and >1.3 indicate duplication. Nomenclature is based on DMD reference sequence LRG_199t1 (Leiden Open Variation Database).

RESULTS
DMD Gene Analysis (LRG_199t1):
- Deletion detected: Exons 49-52
- Gene dosage quotients: Exon 49 (0.02), Exon 50 (0.01), Exon 51 (0.03), Exon 52 (0.01)
- All other exons showed normal copy number (quotients 0.85-1.15)
- Deletion type: Out-of-frame
- Predicted protein effect: Premature termination of dystrophin synthesis

INTERPRETATION
The MLPA analysis identified a deletion of exons 49-52 in the DMD gene. This deletion disrupts the reading frame and is predicted to result in premature termination of dystrophin protein synthesis. Out-of-frame deletions in the DMD gene typically result in absent or severely reduced dystrophin expression, leading to the severe Duchenne muscular dystrophy phenotype.

This deletion is a well-documented pathogenic variant associated with Duchenne muscular dystrophy (den Dunnen et al., 2016; Aartsma-Rus et al., 2016). The deletion of exons 49-52 represents approximately 4% of all DMD deletions reported in the Leiden DMD mutation database.

SUMMARY
MLPA testing confirms the diagnosis of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy in this patient due to an out-of-frame deletion of DMD exons 49-52. This X-linked recessive condition is associated with progressive muscle weakness, typically presenting in early childhood with delayed motor milestones, frequent falls, and difficulty climbing stairs. The condition progresses to loss of ambulation by early teens and cardiac/respiratory complications in young adulthood.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Genetics referral is strongly recommended to discuss the implications of this diagnosis for the patient and family
2. Carrier testing should be offered to the patient's mother and other at-risk female relatives, as carriers may have mild symptoms and are at risk for having affected sons
3. Prenatal diagnosis and preimplantation genetic testing are available for future pregnancies in the family
4. Consider enrollment in the Duchenne Registry (www.duchenneregistry.org) for access to clinical trials and research updates
5. Multidisciplinary care including neurology, cardiology, pulmonology, and physical therapy is recommended
6. Corticosteroid therapy should be discussed with the treating neurologist as per current care standards

REFERENCES
1. den Dunnen JT et al. (2016) DMD gene mutations and the dystrophinopathies. Hum Mutat 37:1-15
2. Aartsma-Rus A et al. (2016) The importance of genetic diagnosis for Duchenne muscular dystrophy. J Med Genet 53:145-151
3. Birnkrant DJ et al. (2018) Diagnosis and management of Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Lancet Neurol 17:251-267

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the FDA. The laboratory is certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity testing.
